Multi-tenant app: each organisation is a tenant, its members hold a role in it, and every project belongs to one organisation. A signed-in user founds an organisation with POST /api/_groups/create and becomes its `org_admin`; that admin adds existing accounts with POST /api/org/members; members read and write only their own organisation's projects, and only an `org_admin` or `manager` deletes one.

content:
# Multi-tenant app: each organisation is a tenant, its members hold a role in
# it, and every project belongs to one organisation.
site_name: "Team projects"
auth:
  identifier: email
groups:
  table: org_members            # one row per member of an organisation
  key: org_id                   # the tenant column on every tenant table
  user_field: user_id
  role_field: member_role       # the member's role inside the organisation
  bootstrap:
    org_table: organizations    # POST /api/_groups/create founds one
    founding_role: org_admin
access:
  organizations:
    read: member-of:org_members(org_id, user_id)   # members read their own organisation
    write: off                  # founded only through /api/_groups/create
    update: role:org_admin
    delete: off
  org_members:
    read: group                 # the roster of the caller's organisation
    write: off                  # added by the bootstrap and flows/add-member.yaml only
    update: off
    delete: role:org_admin
  projects:
    read: group                 # every member of the organisation
    write: group
    update: group
    delete: role:org_admin,manager

model Organization {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  name      String
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  @@map("organizations")
}

model OrgMember {
  id         Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  orgId      Int      @map("org_id")
  userId     Int      @map("user_id")
  memberRole String   @default("member") @map("member_role")
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  @@unique([orgId, userId])
  @@map("org_members")
}

model Project {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  orgId     Int      @map("org_id")
  name      String
  userId    Int      @map("user_id")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  @@map("projects")
}

check: As a new user, POST /api/_groups/create {name} answers 200 {status:'created', group_id, founding_role:'org_admin'} and a second call 409. GET /api/projects, GET /api/organizations and GET /api/org_members list only the caller's organisation; another tenant's row answers 404, and so does a POST to /api/org_members. A `member` creates and edits projects, and gets 403 {error:'forbidden'} on DELETE and on PATCH of the organisation. POST /api/org/members {email, role} answers 201 for the admin, 403 {error:'not_org_admin'} for anyone else, 404 for an unknown address, 409 for a member, and 422 for a role outside `member` and `manager`.
notes: Membership is keyed by user id (`user_field: user_id`), so generic CRUD cannot write another user's membership row: the flow adds the member after checking the caller's own role (`scoping.membership_management`).
Flow SQL does not add the tenant key: the flow binds `org_id` from `${{ user.group_id }}` itself (`flows.gotchas_sql_steps`).

`write: off` on the organisation table leaves /api/_groups/create as the only way to found one, and on the membership table leaves the flow as the only way to add a member. `role:org_admin` on the organisation table reaches only the caller's own organisation row (`access.tenant_root_role_scope`).
The enum on `role` is what stops an admin's request from granting `org_admin`; change a member's role in a flow of the same shape.
